landmarks.name: Ciudad Perdida
landmarks.writeup: An ancient archaeological site in the Sierra Nevada, believed to be older than Machu Picchu.

wiki.extract: Ciudad Perdida is the archaeological site of an ancient city in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta of Colombia, within the jurisdiction of the municipality of Santa Marta. This city is believed to have been founded about 800 AD. If so, Ciudad Perdida predates Machu Picchu by about 650 years. It was built by the Tairona.

landmarks.name: Cartagena's Walled City
landmarks.writeup: A historic colonial city known for its preserved fortifications and vibrant culture.

wiki.extract: Cartagena, known since the imperial era as Cartagena de Indias, is a city and one of the major ports on the northern coast of Colombia in the Caribbean Coast Region, along the Caribbean Sea. Cartagena's past role as a link in the route to the West Indies provides it with important historical value for world exploration and preservation of heritage from the great commercial maritime routes. As a former Spanish colony, it was a key port for the export of Bolivian silver to Spain and for the import of enslaved Africans under the asiento system. It was defensible against pirate attacks in the Caribbean. The city's strategic location between the Magdalena and Sinú rivers also gave it easy access to the interior of New Granada and made it a main port for trade between Spain and its overseas empire, establishing its importance by the early 1540s.

landmarks.name: Tayrona National Natural Park
landmarks.writeup: A coastal park with diverse ecosystems, including beaches, rainforest, and archaeological sites.

wiki.extract: The Tayrona National Natural Park is a protected area in the Colombian northern Caribbean region and within the jurisdiction of the city of Santa Marta, 34 kilometres (21 mi) from the city centre. The park presents a biodiversity endemic to the area of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta mountain range, featuring a variety of climates and geography that ranges from arid sea level to 900 meters above sea level. The park covers approximately 30 square kilometres (12 sq mi) of maritime area in the Caribbean Sea and approximately 150 square kilometres (58 sq mi) of land.

landmarks.name: Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá
landmarks.writeup: An underground Roman Catholic church built within the tunnels of a salt mine.

wiki.extract: The Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá is an underground Roman Catholic church built within the tunnels of a salt mine 200 metres (660 ft) underground in a halite mountain near the city of Zipaquirá, in Cundinamarca, Colombia. It is a tourist destination and place of pilgrimage in the country.

landmarks.name: Monserrate
landmarks.writeup: A mountain overlooking Bogotá, featuring a church and panoramic city views.

wiki.extract: Monserrate is a mountain over 3,000 metres high that overlooks the city center of Bogotá, the capital city of Colombia. It rises to 3,152 meters (10,341 ft) above the sea level, where there is a church with a shrine, devoted to El Señor Caído.

cultural_events.name: Carnaval de Barranquilla
cultural_events.writeup: One of the biggest carnivals in Colombia, showcasing traditional music, dance, and colorful parades.

cultural_events.name: Festival Vallenato
cultural_events.writeup: A festival celebrating vallenato music, a traditional Colombian genre originating from the Caribbean region.

cultural_events.name: Feria de las Flores
cultural_events.writeup: An annual flower festival in Medellín featuring parades, concerts, and cultural exhibitions.

food_writeup: Colombian cuisine is diverse, featuring dishes like arepas, bandeja paisa, empanadas, and a variety of tropical fruits, reflecting its regional diversity and indigenous, Spanish, and African influences.
brief_history: Colombia was inhabited by indigenous peoples before Spanish colonization in the 16th century. It gained independence in 1819. The country has a history of political conflict but has made significant progress in peace and economic development in recent decades.

important_people.name: Simón Bolívar
important_people.description: Military and political leader instrumental in independence

important_people.name: Juan Manuel Santos
important_people.description: Former president and Nobel Peace Prize laureate

current_conflicts: Colombia continues to face challenges related to armed groups, drug trafficking, and social inequality, despite ongoing peace efforts and negotiations.
